acceptance.content: These Terms of Service form a binding agreement between you and IPEACE Professional Consulting ('IPEACE', 'we', or 'us') when you access our website, book a consultation, or engage our business consulting services. You must provide accurate personal and company information, supply requested documents promptly, and remain responsible for decisions and statutory filings made on your behalf. Infringe intellectual property, privacy, or confidentiality rights

After full payment, you may use deliverables prepared for you for your internal business purposes. You may not reproduce, resell, or publicly distribute our materials without prior written consent.

termination.content: Either party may end an engagement by written notice. We may suspend or terminate access immediately if you breach these terms, fail to pay agreed fees, or use our services unlawfully. You remain responsible for fees and approved disbursements for work completed up to the termination date. Provisions concerning intellectual property, confidentiality, and liability survive termination.

disclaimer.content: Website content is general business and compliance information, not legal, tax, investment, or other advice tailored to your circumstances. Except for rights that cannot be excluded under Zimbabwe's Consumer Protection Act [Chapter 14:44], our online services are provided on an 'as is' and 'as available' basis.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.content: IPEACE Professional Consulting respects your privacy and processes personal information in accordance with Zimbabwe's Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07]. For the purposes of that Act, IPEACE is the data controller for the information described in this policy. The Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Zimbabwe (POTRAZ) is the national data protection authority.

personal.title: Personal and Business Information
personal.content: We collect information that you provide when making an inquiry, booking a consultation, registering for the client portal, or engaging our services, including:
examples: Names, identification details, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses
Company registration, director, shareholder, tax, and licensing information
Consultation records, project documents, and correspondence

usage.title: Technical and Usage Information
usage.content: When you use our website, we may automatically collect limited technical information, including:
examples: Browser type, operating system, and device information
IP address, approximate location, and access timestamps
Pages visited, actions taken, and time spent on our website

howWeUseInformation.title: How and Why We Use Your Information
howWeUseInformation.content: We process personal information only where we have a lawful basis, such as your consent, performance of a contract, compliance with a legal obligation, or our legitimate business interests. We use it to:
purposes: Provide, administer, and improve our consulting services
Respond to inquiries and manage consultation bookings
Send service updates and marketing communications where permitted, with consent where required
Prepare registrations, filings, and other instructions you ask us to perform
Meet tax, accounting, companies, anti-money-laundering, and other legal obligations
Secure our systems, prevent misuse, and understand website performance

dataProtection.title: Data Security and Breach Handling
dataProtection.content: We use appropriate technical and organisational safeguards, including access controls and secure transmission, to protect personal information against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure. Only authorised personnel and service providers may access it for the purposes in this policy. Where required by the Cyber and Data Protection Act, we will notify POTRAZ and affected data subjects of a qualifying personal data breach.

sharingOfInformation.title: Sharing and Cross-Border Processing
sharingOfInformation.content: We do not sell or rent personal information. We may disclose it only in these circumstances, using contractual or other appropriate safeguards where information is processed outside Zimbabwe:
cases: With trusted hosting, email, payment, and other service providers acting on our instructions
With courts, law enforcement, ZIMRA, the Deeds Registry, or other authorities where required or authorised by law
With professional advisers or a successor in a merger, restructuring, or business transfer, subject to confidentiality
With your explicit consent or at your direction for a specific purpose

yourRights.title: Your Data Protection Rights
yourRights.content: Subject to the Cyber and Data Protection Act and applicable exceptions, you may exercise the rights below by contacting us. You may also withdraw consent at any time without affecting earlier lawful processing, and lodge a complaint with POTRAZ if you believe your information has been handled unlawfully:
rights: Request access to and a copy of your personal information
Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete information
Request deletion where the information is no longer lawfully required
Object to or request restriction of certain processing, including direct marketing
Request portability of information you provided, where technically and legally applicable

dataRetention.title: Data Retention
dataRetention.content: We retain personal information only for as long as needed for the purpose collected, our engagement with you, and applicable limitation, tax, accounting, and company-record obligations. When it is no longer required, we securely delete, destroy, or anonymise it.

Where we use optional analytics or similar technologies, we do so subject to applicable consent requirements. You can control or delete cookies through your browser settings, although blocking essential cookies may affect the client portal and other features.

thirdPartyLinks.content: Our website may link to third-party websites or services. Their processing is governed by their own privacy policies, and IPEACE is not responsible for their content or practices. Please review those policies before providing personal information.

childrenPrivacy.content: Our services are intended for businesses and adults aged 18 or older. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Zimbabwe Business Compliance
faq.subtitle: Get answers to common questions about starting and running a business in Zimbabwe

questions.question: How do I register a company in Zimbabwe?
questions.answer: To register a company in Zimbabwe, you need to: 1) Choose a unique company name, 2) Prepare Memorandum and Articles of Association, 3) File with the Companies Office, 4) Obtain a tax clearance certificate, and 5) Register for VAT if applicable. Our system can guide you through each step.

questions.question: What are the requirements for company compliance in Zimbabwe?
questions.answer: Zimbabwe companies must comply with: Companies Act Chapter 24:03, annual returns filing, director's reports, audited financial statements, tax compliance, and industry-specific regulations. We provide comprehensive compliance checklists and monitoring.

questions.question: How much does it cost to register a company in Zimbabwe?
questions.answer: Company registration costs vary by type: Private companies (~$50-200 USD), Public companies (~$500+ USD), plus additional costs for legal fees, tax clearance, and business licenses. We offer cost-effective registration packages with all required documentation.

questions.question: What business licenses do I need in Zimbabwe?
questions.answer: Required licenses depend on your business type: Trading License from local council, Tax Clearance Certificate, VAT registration (if turnover >$60,000), Specific industry licenses (mining, tourism, etc.). We help identify and obtain all necessary licenses.

questions.question: How can we help with Zimbabwe business compliance?
questions.answer: We provide: 24/7 compliance monitoring, automated document analysis, regulatory updates, risk assessment, instant legal queries, and predictive compliance insights trained on Zimbabwe's legal framework.

questions.question: What are the penalties for non-compliance in Zimbabwe?
questions.answer: Penalties include fines up to $500,000, imprisonment up to 5 years, business closure, director disqualification, and reputational damage. We help businesses maintain 99.8% compliance rate through proactive monitoring.
